items.headline: Flood Warning issued May 5 at 4:34PM AKDT until May 6 at 4:30PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
The ice has stopped at Eagle, water levels are approaching road
level between town and village, flooding may occur if the ice
continues to back up water.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by an ice jam may occur.

* WHERE...Yukon River near Eagle, Ak.

* WHEN...Until 430 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding as well as large blocks of ice being pushed
onshore. Water will remain high until the ice jam releases.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

Bluffs. In-place ice shows signs of weakening but the

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued May 5 at 2:27PM AKDT until May 7 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Snow and blowing snow expected. Total snow accumulations
between 1 to 3 inches. Winds gusting as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Areas of blowing snow could
reduce visibility to a quarter mile at times.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...After a lull in winds this afternoon,
westerly winds will pick up by Tuesday evening and continue
through Thursday.
items.instruction: Slow down and use caution while traveling.

items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by an ice jam is possible.

* WHERE...From Crooked Creek to below Napaimute.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday evening.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 5 at 8:01AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
As a front pushes across the Brooks Range, snow totals of around 4
to 7 inches will be possible across the Central Arctic Coast,
especially between Utqiagvik and Nuiqsut, and the Central Arctic
Plains. The highest snowfall rates are likely to occur from
Tuesday night through Wednesday afternoon. Along the Dalton
